description: Normative CodeScope contract reference. These contracts make the behavior required by the directives explicit without making implementation or tests authoritative.

authority.implementationRole: Implementation files realize these contracts but cannot redefine them.
authority.verificationRole: Tests and commands verify these contracts but are not authoritative.

terminology.contract: One cohesive externally observable behavior owned by CodeScope.
terminology.directiveId: A local E- or A-prefixed directive identifier that gives authority context.
terminology.implementationEvidence: Source ownership references used to locate realization of a contract; not normative.
terminology.verificationEvidence: Tests and commands used to verify a contract; not normative.

rules: Contract IDs are unique within this repository.
directiveIds reference authoritative local directives or explicitly linked external directives.
Parent and dependency references must resolve and must not form cycles.
Implementation and verification references are evidence only.
This repository adopts the shared format by linking specs/contracts.json from specs/README.md.

contracts.title: CLI entry and command dispatch
contracts.scope: Process entry, command dispatch, and CodeScope-owned CLI boundaries.

contract.purpose: Define CodeScope's public command boundary and review dispatch.
contract.inputs: The current working directory and command-line arguments.
contract.outputs: Help, version, review, suggestion, prompt, usage, or dry-run behavior selected by the command.
errors: Invalid command usage and CodeScope-owned execution failures are nonzero process failures.
ordering: Parse command metadata before dispatching profile work.

dos: Treat the current working directory as the review root.
Default a bare invocation to the single help page.
Support help, version, prompt, grouped review and suggestion commands, direct profile shorthand, usage, dry-run, model, effort, and repeatable add options.
Keep bin/codescope.mjs limited to process wiring and route behavior through the CLI modules.
donts: Do not modify the reviewed repository or run its commands.
Do not make command dispatch depend on provider response content.
Do not add deployment, publication, synchronization, commit, push, or release behavior.

contracts.title: Argument and option semantics
contracts.scope: Command-line option parsing and repeatable custom additions.

contract.purpose: Define supported CodeScope options and their interactions.
contract.inputs: Command-line tokens including repeatable -a/--add, --effort, and --model options.
contract.outputs: A normalized command representation preserving applicable additions in order.
errors: Missing option values and unsupported values produce usage failures.
ordering: Added strings retain command-line order and are appended at the final user-message boundary.
invariants: Bare, help, and version commands do not apply additions.

dos: Accept -a and --add with a required string value, preserve each value verbatim, and preserve command-line order.
Treat non-option tokens as free-form prompt text for codescope prompt; use -- when prompt text itself begins with a dash.
Use the shared scalar option parser for effort, model, dry-run, and additions; prompt-specific delimiter partitioning is intentional grammar, not a second scalar option contract.
Normalize direct and grouped scalar options through one scanner before profile-specific validation.
Allow add options on profile commands including all, release, review profiles, suggestion profiles, and prompt.
Accept add options on bare, help, and version commands without changing their output; retain accepted additions in normalized metadata so acceptance is not silent loss.
Reject malformed option values with a usage error and keep supported effort and model values explicit.
donts: Do not apply added text to bare, help, or version output.
Do not normalize, merge, reorder, summarize, or silently discard added text.
Do not treat an added prompt as a replacement for the profile prompt.

contracts.title: Profiles and source selection
contracts.scope: Review and suggestion profile identity, routing, and selected evidence.

contract.purpose: Define profile selection and source scope for a review.
contract.inputs: A declared profile name and review or suggestion mode.
contract.outputs: A profile prompt and source-selection function for the requested mode.
errors: Unknown profiles and unsupported modes fail explicitly.
ordering: Resolve profile mode before selecting evidence and decorating prompts.
invariants: Suggestion profiles do not become blocking review profiles.

dos: Keep review and suggestion modes distinct while allowing the declared profile set: conventions, refactor, architecture, new-features, all, release, security, performance, reliability, api-design, cross-platform, dependencies, observability, accessibility, quick-wins, prioritize, p0, p0-1, p0-2, and p0-3.
Use the all operation for comprehensive implementation, test, documentation, metadata, and remaining-file evidence.
Route suggest all through one generic non-blocking suggestion prompt covering every review category plus new-features.
Use prompt with the all context and no review or suggestion tool requirement.
Keep new-features in suggestion mode when invoked through the review command.
donts: Do not silently map an unknown profile to a valid profile.
Do not use suggestion profiles as blocking review profiles.
Do not make profile selection alter the read-only repository boundary.

contracts.title: Evidence discovery and repository safety
contracts.scope: Read-only file discovery, path safety, symlink handling, and evidence exclusions.

contract.purpose: Define safe discovery of review evidence without mutating the reviewed repository.
contract.inputs: A review root and filesystem entries.
contract.outputs: Safe, deterministic supplied-file candidates and unknown markers for unavailable evidence.
errors: Invalid roots, unsafe paths, and unsupported filesystem conditions fail without repository mutation.
ordering: Validate boundaries before reading file contents.
invariants: Symbolic-link targets, dependencies, Git metadata, and generated coverage data are not followed or supplied.

dos: Read supplied files without executing repository code or commands.
Skip dependency directories, Git metadata, generated coverage data, and symbolic-link targets.
Retain legitimate source directories named coverage when they are not generated artifacts.
Treat absent, excluded, symbolic-link, or unsupplied evidence as unknown rather than inventing facts.
Preserve path-boundary and concurrency validation before file side effects.
donts: Do not follow symbolic links into targets.
Do not include credentials, runtime state, or test execution results as if they were supplied evidence.
Do not write fixes, commits, or other changes to the reviewed repository.

contracts.title: Evidence composition and budgets
contracts.scope: Composition order, content selection, aggregate limits, and metadata accounting.

contract.purpose: Define deterministic composition and size limits for supplied review evidence.
contract.inputs: Selected repository evidence and configured character or byte limits.
contract.outputs: One ordered combined evidence string or an explicit budget failure.
errors: Aggregate limits fail deterministically when actual content exceeds the configured budget.
ordering: Package, Convention, JSON, configuration, other-file metadata, Markdown, implementation, and tests follow the declared order.
invariants: Each other file is limited independently to 100000 bytes based on a reader result containing data and an explicit truncated flag; metadata reads use bounded concurrency and preserve sorted output.

dos: Compose comprehensive evidence in the documented order: package metadata, applicable Convention JSON, eligible JSON, configuration, other-file metadata, Markdown, implementation, and tests.
Exclude package-lock.json from JSON evidence and exclude Convention package metadata and lockfiles.
Limit configuration text to 200 lines and enforce the 100000-byte per-file metadata limit.
Read no more than one byte beyond the 100000-byte per-file limit, return the bytes with an explicit truncated flag, and omit only the file that exceeds its limit.
Use one shared aggregate section-joining limit for all and selected composition paths.
donts: Do not stat files before reading them, infer overflow from a short injected prefix, serialize all metadata reads unnecessarily, or use a shared metadata budget that lets one file omit unrelated later files.
Do not apply different per-file limits to all and selected composition.
Do not treat metadata summaries as full file contents.

contracts.title: Convention evidence boundary
contracts.scope: Selection and supply of canonical Convention records as review evidence.

contract.purpose: Define how CodeScope consumes convention evidence without redefining convention policy.
contract.inputs: package.json Convention applicability and the adjacent conventions checkout.
contract.outputs: Only applicable canonical Convention JSON records or an explicit unavailable/incomplete-evidence marker.
errors: Missing or malformed applicability is reported as unavailable rather than inferred.
ordering: Read applicability before selecting canonical records.
invariants: CodeScope does not redefine Convention requirements.

dos: Read only the repository types declared by package.json eliware.conventions.apply.
Load canonical Convention JSON from the adjacent conventions checkout.
Report the checkout, applicability, or applied record as unavailable when it cannot be supplied.
Treat canonical Conventions records as the authority for repository requirements.
donts: Do not redefine, duplicate, or extend Convention requirements in CodeScope contracts.
Do not infer Convention requirements when canonical evidence is unavailable.
Do not treat CodeScope's convention-evidence behavior as authority over repository structure.

contracts.title: Prompt and tool contracts
contracts.scope: Prompt composition, profile guidance, tool schemas, priorities, and supplied-evidence instructions.

contract.purpose: Define prompt construction and tool-request boundaries for review providers.
contract.inputs: Selected profile, supplied evidence, optional custom additions, and prompt options.
contract.outputs: Provider request instructions and optional tool definitions.
errors: Prompt construction failures remain CodeScope-owned failures.
ordering: System and profile guidance precede evidence; additions are appended to the final user message.
invariants: Provider output is not locally accepted or rejected by these prompt contracts.

dos: Keep system guidance, identity, evidence, priorities, scope, transport, and profile guidance as separate cohesive prompt responsibilities.
Request independent secret review and P0/P1 blocking recommendations from the provider where the profile requires it.
Keep tool schemas and provider instructions as requested-output guidance, not local acceptance requirements.
Append custom additions to the final user message after the normal profile content.
donts: Do not parse or validate successful provider output against a local response schema.
Do not turn prompt guidance into repository enforcement or automatic remediation.
Do not claim redaction or AI inspection is a complete secret-removal boundary.

contracts.title: Provider transport and raw output
contracts.scope: Provider request execution, output preservation, write completion, and safe failure summaries.

contract.purpose: Define provider invocation and preservation of raw provider output.
contract.inputs: A prepared provider request, cancellation signal, and output writer.
contract.outputs: The exact successful provider response text or a provider failure with preserved diagnostics.
errors: Transport failures and incomplete output writes are nonzero CodeScope-owned failures.
ordering: Collect and validate local repository evidence before provider setup; complete provider execution before writing the result; cleanup follows success or failure.
invariants: Successful provider output is not parsed, formatted, or transformed.

dos: Send the prepared request to the provider and preserve the exact successful response text unchanged.
Allow review, suggestion, and custom-prompt responses to remain provider-defined and non-machine-readable.
Preserve safe diagnostic summaries when a provider response cannot be serialized.
Report provider transport failures and output-write failures with their original error context.

Accept writer results of undefined, true, or an object with an exact written character count; the default stdout adapter intentionally discards Node stream backpressure booleans and the count is measured in JavaScript characters, not bytes.
Use an explicit common internal session-result shape for dry-run and provider sessions while returning the output at the public pipeline boundary.
donts: Do not parse, validate, redact, pretty-print, format, or transform successful provider output.
Do not derive process status or exit code from provider content.
Do not discard all safe function-call summaries because one provider call is malformed.
Do not accept false, numbers, strings, null, or unrelated objects as writer results.
Do not treat a short explicit writer count as a successful complete write.

contracts.title: Configuration and credential safety
contracts.scope: Credential loading, environment-file safety, Unix modes, and Windows ACL restrictions.

contract.purpose: Define configuration precedence and credential-handling safety.
contract.inputs: Process environment, ~/.codescope, platform permission evidence, and injected filesystem seams.
contract.outputs: A validated environment for provider setup or an explicit safety failure.
errors: Unsafe permissions, symbolic links, unstable races, missing credentials, and inspection failures are handled explicitly.
ordering: Inspect configuration safety before accepting its contents.
invariants: A nonblank process token wins; a missing or whitespace-only process token is absent and may be replaced by a nonblank file token.
Permission validation is enabled by default and is disabled only by an explicit false option.

dos: Use a nonblank OPENAI_API_TOKEN from the process environment when present; otherwise read ~/.codescope and use its nonblank token.
Reject symbolic-link configuration files.
On Unix, reject group/world-readable configuration files.

On Windows, obtain a machine-readable SDDL descriptor through PowerShell's .NET security APIs, pass only the required process variables and target path to the child rather than the full credential-bearing environment, and require every parsed DACL ACE to be an allow ACE for only the current user SID.

Default the environment reader to the configured file reader, treat a missing optional configuration file as empty when the initial read also reports absence, and if it appears during startup use the read contents without a second appearance check.
Preserve provider credentials outside the reviewed repository.
donts: Do not treat a missing or whitespace-only process token as authoritative over a nonblank file token.
Do not parse localized human-readable ACL output or accept an unverified, malformed, or unknown-SID Windows ACL as restricted.
Do not silently accept a file that disappears, is replaced, or changes safety state during the permission check.
Do not place credentials, tokens, environment files, or runtime state in the repository.

contracts.title: Usage, pricing, and dry-run behavior
contracts.scope: Model and effort options, token estimation, usage metadata, and pricing calculations.

contract.purpose: Define usage accounting, pricing display, and dry-run semantics.
contract.inputs: A selected model, request, usage flag, and dry-run flag.
contract.outputs: Estimated input tokens or requested usage and cost metadata.
errors: Unsupported model, effort, or usage inputs fail explicitly.
ordering: Dry-run estimates input tokens without executing a model review.
invariants: No output-token usage is fabricated for dry-run requests.

dos: Support model selection and effort selection through the documented values.
Use dry-run to estimate input tokens without running a model review.
Include usage metadata and calculated cost only when requested.
Normalize provider usage and use the selected model's pricing thresholds.
donts: Do not run a model review during dry-run.
Do not fabricate output-token usage when no output was generated.
Do not let usage or pricing metadata alter provider response text.

contracts.title: Errors, exit codes, and lifecycle
contracts.scope: CodeScope-owned failures, public exit behavior, cancellation, and cleanup.

contract.purpose: Define failure propagation, exit status, and lifecycle cleanup.
contract.inputs: Command execution results, provider results, failures, signals, and cleanup callbacks.
contract.outputs: A stable success or CodeScope-owned nonzero exit result with preserved error context.
errors: Provider verdicts and finding priorities never become process failures.
ordering: Abort active work and remove signal handlers after success or failure.
invariants: The original provider or writer failure remains observable.

dos: Use nonzero exit codes for CodeScope-owned failures such as invalid CLI usage, missing credentials, provider transport failures, unsafe configuration, and output-write failures.
Return success after a provider response regardless of its verdict, finding priorities, schema, or formatting.
Abort provider work and remove signal handlers during normal completion and failure cleanup.
Preserve error causes and safe fallback metadata.
donts: Do not make an AI verdict, P0/P1 finding, or provider JSON content change the process exit code.
Do not leave signal handlers or provider work active after completion.
Do not hide the original provider or writer failure behind an unrelated cleanup error.

contracts.title: Module, dependency, and verification boundaries
contracts.scope: Cohesive module responsibilities, shared dependencies, mirrored tests, and verification boundaries.

contract.purpose: Define CodeScope module boundaries and the evidence used to verify them.
contract.inputs: Production modules, package metadata, and verification tooling.
contract.outputs: Maintainable native ESM modules with traceable, comprehensive verification.
errors: Coverage, lint, formatting, and diff failures remain verification failures rather than contract redefinitions.
ordering: Implement contract behavior before relying on verification evidence.
invariants: Implementation and tests are evidence only; normative contract changes occur in specs.

dos: Keep production modules cohesive with one meaningful responsibility and explicit orchestration at composition boundaries.
Use native ESM and Node process APIs with argument arrays rather than shell-specific command construction.
Use the maintained shared Eliware packages for their owned capabilities and keep public exports and package metadata synchronized.
Mirror source modules with tests under tests/ and use tests as evidence that the normative contracts are fulfilled.
Assume the full repository test suite passes unless concrete failing-test evidence is supplied; review test files for contract coverage without requiring execution output.
Maintain full in-scope statement, branch, function, and line coverage without Istanbul ignores outside pure barrels.
donts: Do not make tests the source of contract truth.
Do not report missing test execution output or infer a test failure that was not supplied.
Do not hide independent responsibilities in monolithic modules or comments.
Do not add shell-specific pipelines, platform-specific executable assumptions, or duplicate maintained-library functionality without a documented exception.
